parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grieving parent is let down by a daughter's absence when a man died.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes that are dashed are crushed, so a dashed person is someone left feeling let down.

parts.note: Di's, the possessive of the girl's name Di
diamonds is one suit of playing cards

explanation.surface: A woman gets rid of her jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: Diamonds looks like jewels; it is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard is to get rid of something, especially an unwanted playing card.

indicators.note: the letters of bulbs lay are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plate of flower bulbs has been strewn about.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed key reads SYLLABUS, but the anagram and the definition both give the dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabub is an old English dessert of whipped cream with wine or sherry.

parts.note: the answer is inside these words, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A punter learns the following horse race offers additional prize money.
explanation.walkthrough: Yields signals that the words give up the answer they contain.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is an additional item, something given over and above what is expected.

clue.text: Drop, or dropped, from the general discussion

indicators.note: the clue's own word or is let fall out of the longer phrase, so those two letters go

parts.note: a free-for-all is an open argument in which everyone joins in
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a topic should be raised or abandoned in an open meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop and dropped look like one idea repeated; the first is the definition, the second tells you to drop the little word or.
explanation.definitionFit: A free fall is an unchecked plunge, as of a skydiver before the parachute opens, so a sheer descent.

clue.text: It has its ups and downs

definitions.text: It has its ups and downs

parts.note: sounds like a remark about life or a relationship
the literal climbs and drops of a fairground ride

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a stock comment on life's mixed fortunes; taken literally, it describes a fairground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller coaster is a fairground ride on a track of steep climbs and plunges.

indicators.note: almost all of the word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: refers to the answer to 3 down
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person counts as lively when nearly over the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The 3 points to the answer of 3 down, used here as a building block.
explanation.definitionFit: An extrovert is outgoing and sociable, a personality full of animation and energy.

parts.note: taken as written
a tease is a playful joke at someone's expense

explanation.surface: Someone is calm, thanks to a bit of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at ease is to feel comfortable and free from tension.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the most tardy, superlative of late

explanation.walkthrough: The surface contrasts fast modernity with slowness; both are senses of one superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest is the newest, and also the one who arrives after everyone else.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to divide something between people
second meaning: a banana ..., a dessert of a halved banana with ice cream

explanation.surface: An invitation to divide a dessert between two diners.
explanation.definitionFit: To split a bill is to share it, and a banana split is a well-known fruit dessert.

parts.note: reads like economic expansion, but means plants grown in soil
a plot of land rather than a business sector

explanation.surface: Business jargon for a sector of the economy that is expanding.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a stock economics term; read literally, it is a rented patch of ground where vegetables grow.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a small rented plot of land, common in Britain, where people grow vegetables and flowers.

clue.text: Unfortunate way of speaking I'd fallen into prior to lying

indicators.note: places the speaking-and-I'd unit before the word for lying
the word for I'd has dropped inside the way of speaking

parts.note: an accent is a manner of pronunciation
taken as written, without the apostrophe
prone means lying face down

explanation.surface: Someone admits slipping into an awkward manner of speech before telling lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone accident-prone keeps suffering mishaps, so is habitually unlucky.

clue.text: Fall for a girl he can change

parts.note: taken as written
Val is a short girl's name

indicators.note: the letters of he can are to be changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Falling for a girl is something a man can change his mind about.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall looks like falling in love; it is the definition, a fall of snow down a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a sudden fall of snow and ice down a mountainside.

clue.text: Nothing is as moving as a safe haven

parts.note: O is the zero digit, nothing

indicators.note: the letters of is as are moved around into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nothing touches the heart like finding a place of safety.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile refuge in a desert, and figuratively any peaceful retreat.

clue.text: Vehicle turned by church, reversing against unfinished pavement

parts.note: to double back is to turn round, so doubled can mean turned

indicators.note: the abbreviation for church is read backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for pavement edge is left off

parts.note: a kerb is the edge of a pavement (British spelling of curb)

explanation.surface: A car swerves past a church, backing up against a half-built footpath.
explanation.walkthrough: KERB is the British spelling of curb, the raised edge of a pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-decker is a bus with two passenger levels, the classic London bus.

clue.text: Official found Romola dry in new version

indicators.note: the letters of Romola dry are rewritten in another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written; Romola is a George Eliot novel

explanation.surface: A civic dignitary turns up in a fresh, dry adaptation of George Eliot's novel Romola.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lord Mayor is the ceremonial head of a city council in Britain, such as London.

parts.note: feeling down means feeling blue
a turn is an act in a variety show

explanation.surface: Reviewers note the falling standard of a risqué stage act.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue looks like risqué, as in blue comedy; it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a fall in activity, especially an economic slump.

clue.text: Has the means to mess about during get together

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit within the word for having the means

parts.note: to be able is to have the means

indicators.note: the letters of mess are moved about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People with resources fool around while meeting up.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather in one place, as a group meets together.

clue.text: Drawing up exceptional sanctions against trading

indicators.note: in a down clue... here up signals that the word for drawing is read backwards

parts.note: drawing is a form of art

indicators.note: exceptional suggests unusual, so the letters of sanctions take an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Officials are drafting unusual sanctions to stop commerce with a country.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawing up looks like drafting the sanctions; drawing is the art, turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Transactions are business deals, so the plural noun covers buying and selling activity.

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the recorded word goes round the piano

parts.note: taped means recorded on tape

explanation.surface: A hit song was recorded with no piano part.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like lacking; here it means outside, so the piano sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap is to strike lightly, so tapped means struck.

parts.note: sounds like a frying pan coating
the reward offered in place of punishment

explanation.walkthrough: Non-stick suggests cookware; it alludes to the carrot-and-stick choice between reward and punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is a reward dangled to motivate, contrasted with the stick of punishment.

clue.text: Panic caused by a student with weapon

parts.note: taken as written
L is a learner driver, a student
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: Fear spreads when a student turns up carrying a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or anxiety, so it means much the same as panic.

clue.text: Sulky behaviour shown by girl once a non-starter

parts.note: Petula is a girl's name, as in the singer Petula Clark

indicators.note: once must go without its starting letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl's sulking is attributed to her having once been a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-starter looks like a hopeless person; it tells you to remove the first letter of once.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is childish bad temper, the peevish sulking of someone who did not get their way.

clue.text: Pale design on left part of garment

indicators.note: the letters of pale are redesigned into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A light-coloured pattern appears on the left side of a piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded flap on the front of a jacket or coat.

clue.text: Invited one to have a bash at live wire

definitions.text: Invited one to have a bash
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a guest at a party, a bash being a party
second meaning: a lively, sociable person

explanation.walkthrough: Have a bash at looks like attempting something; the bash is a party, and at joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest attends a party, and the term also describes a gregarious person who loves socialising.

explanation.walkthrough: On the level looks like honesty; here it means true and straight as a builder's line.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumb is informal for completely, and as an adjective means exactly vertical or true.

parts.note: Det is the abbreviation for detective
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: Someone lost heart when a detective went astray.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deterred is to be put off from acting, so prevented through discouragement.

parts.note: reads as a remarkable appearance, but means a quick look
a glancing blow strikes and slides off, so the word also hits

explanation.walkthrough: A striking look sounds like a beautiful face; the answer is both a brief look and a blow that strikes and bounces off.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a brief look, and as a verb it also describes a blow that strikes obliquely.
